overview: Harden the existing Linux automation scripts for Zotero and a mounted WebDAV folder, with the main synchronizer remaining automatic while failures become testable and explicit.
goals: Keep the main Zotero/WebDAV synchronization path automated once configured.
Make the main synchronizer import-safe so unit tests can exercise helpers without secrets or live API calls.
Add narrow tests around configuration, path, cache, copy, rename, and failure-reporting behavior.
Ensure critical failures are visible in logs, final reports, and process outcomes.
nonGoals: No conversion of support scripts into separate products.
No cross-platform support beyond Linux with mounted WebDAV in the current cycle.
No live Zotero API calls in unit tests.
No manual confirmation prompt in the normal main sync path.
successMetrics: The main sync module can be imported without required environment variables or a mounted WebDAV folder.
Unit tests cover the first hardening seam without contacting Zotero.
Syntax validation passes for all observed Python scripts.
Final reports and exit behavior distinguish critical failures from successful sync completion.
openQuestions: Whether future integration tests should use a fake Zotero server or real opt-in credentials.
Whether the repository should later adopt a package layout after hardening the script boundaries.

stack.hosting: Local Linux automation with mounted WebDAV
stack.database: No database; local JSON hash cache under ~/.cache/zotero_sync_webdav
stack.auth: Zotero API key from environment or env file

importFormat.description: Not applicable. The project processes local PDFs and Zotero API responses rather than importing a user-provided data file.

rules: The main synchronizer remains automatic by default.
Missing secrets, missing WebDAV mount, copy failures, rename failures, and API failures must not be reported as successful sync completion.
Unit tests must not require ZOTERO_API_KEY, a live Zotero account, or a mounted WebDAV folder.
Filesystem mutation helpers must not overwrite existing destination files silently.
Each Ralph cycle executes exactly one story.

stories.title: Make main sync import-safe and testable
stories.description: As a maintainer, I want zotero_sync_webdav.py to be import-safe so tests can exercise pure helpers without secrets, a mounted WebDAV folder, or live Zotero calls.
acceptanceCriteria: Move required-environment validation and runtime-only side effects out of module import and into an explicit runtime path used by main().
Importing zotero_sync_webdav with no ZOTERO_* environment variables does not raise and does not contact Zotero.
Example: a unit test can import normalize_filename, normalize_aggressive, resolve_target_folder, and _coerce_response_items without a .env file.

Negative case: calling the runtime config loader with missing ZOTERO_LIBRARY_ID, ZOTERO_API_KEY, or ZOTERO_SYNC_TARGET_FOLDER returns or raises a clear configuration failure before any Zotero API call.
Add a tests/ suite using the Python standard library unittest module for import-safety, path resolution, filename normalization, and malformed Zotero response coercion.
The quality gates pass: python3 -m py_compile zotero_sync_webdav.py zotero_mirror_collections_to_obsidian.py and python3 -m unittest discover -s tests.

stories.title: Test filesystem mutation helpers
stories.description: As a maintainer, I want copy, rename, and hash-cache helpers covered by temporary-directory tests so file mutation behavior does not regress silently.
acceptanceCriteria: Add unit tests for rename_webdav_file covering successful rename and existing-destination collision.
Add unit tests for copy_to_local_storage covering copied, exists, and copy-failure outcomes without touching the real ~/Zotero/storage directory.
Add unit tests for hash cache lookup and cache entry rename using temporary files.
Example: renaming a WebDAV PDF to an unused canonical name updates the path and cache entry.
Negative case: when the destination filename already exists, the helper does not overwrite it and returns the original path.
The quality gates pass.

stories.title: Add automated preflight checks
stories.description: As an unattended automation user, I want preflight checks to catch missing Linux/WebDAV and local-storage prerequisites before the sync starts mutating Zotero or files.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a preflight function for required config values, WebDAV folder existence, WebDAV readability, local storage writability, and optional desktop tooling availability.
The preflight keeps the main sync automatic; it fails fast with a clear error instead of asking for confirmation.
Example: a mounted readable WebDAV directory and writable local storage allow the sync to proceed.
Negative case: a missing target folder stops before Zotero attachment creation or file rename/copy operations.
Add unit tests for pass and fail preflight cases using temporary directories.
The quality gates pass.

stories.title: Make run outcome truthful
stories.description: As an operator, I want the script's final report and process result to clearly distinguish completed syncs from critical failures.
acceptanceCriteria: Define critical failures for missing config, failed Zotero connection, missing target folder, failed attachment add, failed copy when required, and unexpected processing exceptions.
Ensure main() returns an explicit status or exits nonzero for critical failure while preserving a successful zero-exit path for completed runs.
Example: when Zotero connection fails, the final output records the failure and the process exits nonzero.
Negative case: a run with zero PDFs in an existing target folder exits successfully and reports no work rather than failure.
Add tests for success, no-work, and critical-failure outcome mapping without live Zotero calls.
The quality gates pass.
